milestone.description: Q3 2017: Persistence, Akka IO, Serialization, Documentation, and .NET Core Support.

repository.description: Canonical actor model implementation for .NET with local + distributed actors in C# and F#.

issue.body:
Intermittent issue with the TeamCity build agent preparing to run a build.  When it attempts to clean the checkout directory, it's unable to delete all of the files due to what seems to be a process locking them.  Looks like these files are related to .dlls downloaded to the `.dotnet` folder on the server which are added when we run `dotnet-install.ps1` to download the .NET CLI v1.0.4.

Once there is a failure to clean the checkout directory, all subsequent builds on that specific build agent have the same issue, indicating that the process isn't being killed properly.

Possible solution is to use FAKE's ProcessHelper to 
kill all processes created by FAKE so that the usage of the .NET CLI by build.fsx is killed regardless of the success/failure of the build:

https://github.com/fsharp/FAKE/blob/master/src/app/FakeLib/ProcessHelper.fs#L522:
```
/// Kills all processes that are created by the FAKE build script unless "donotkill" flag was set.
let killAllCreatedProcesses() =
...
```

issue.title: Kill xunit.console explicitly on each dotnet-xunit execution

repository.name: akka.net
repository.description: Canonical actor model implementation for .NET with local + distributed actors in C# and F#.

issue.body:
Seeing `Address already in use` errors occasionally in CI with, for example, Remote.TestKit.Tests and Akka.Streams.Tests.  We implemented a final FAKE Target that kills `xunit.console` after the entire test suite is run, however we aren't ensuring that `xunit.console` process is killed after the `runSingleProject` function in build.fsx per https://github.com/xunit/xunit/issues/1338.  

In v1.2.3 and earlier, the XUnit2 helper from FAKE is using ExecProcess under the hood to kick off `xunit.console.exe` and kills it after each test project is run.  This PR makes the test running consistent with `dev` branch using XUnit2 test helper from FAKE, which did ensure that the xunit process was killed and restarted on a per-project basis.

body: test project takes at least a few 10s of seconds to run, so you can observe the effect. Or, to really demonstrate it convincingly, put an endless loop in one of your tests, to simulate some kind of problem that makes the tests take a long time.

The fix I've added for this is to improve Ctrl+C handling. Now, when the user presses Ctrl+C during one of the `dotnet build` or `msbuild` steps, we see that cancellation and let it bubble up; when the user presses Ctrl+C during `dotnet xunit.console.dll` or `xunit.console.exe`, the existing handlers will be in place (attempting graceful shutdown, but allowing full-on termination with a second press of Ctrl+C). Either way, we see this and stop the process.

I do not intend to add any special logic around non-graceful process termination of `dotnet xunit` itself, as this is not a user scenario we feel is worth addressing. End users will normally use Ctrl+C to terminate a process that they are using interactively.

This will ship in 2.3.1.

issue.title: Jenkins failes to cancel xunit.console run

labels.name: External
labels.description: The issue is caused by an external party

repository.name: xunit
repository.description: xUnit.net is a free, open source, community-focused unit testing tool for .NET.

issue.body:
This issue is similar to #1338. But that was reported to be fixed with 2.3.1 and this error occurs with 2.4.0.

When a build job is canceled, while it currently runs the test , the xunit.console runner is not terminating. This causes the next builds to fail, because the `git clean -fdx`, which we do in the beginning, is failing.

# How to reproduce

1. Have a project where the tests take longer. Our project has ~16k tests and needs ~4 min to run them all.
2. Execute them automatically on Jenkins e.g. on changes to a Github-PR or a Gerrit patchset.
3. Cancel the build manually or automatically (it is common that if you upload a new Gerrit patchset to a change and a build for the same change is running the older one is canceled, because you do not need it any longer)
4. Have a new build running in the same workspace
-> It fails to clean the workspace because of file locks. Also in the process manger of the build node you can see the process still running.

This process will keep running more or less the time it needs to finish the test run regularly. 

# Question

Is this the bug of #1338 and it got added again to 2.4.0? 
Or if everything is working as intended, would it be possible to have a flag for the console runner, which doesn't require 2 times Ctrl-C to be force canceled?
